title: Morning Along the Lane
story:
James woke to the pale gold sunlight filtering through the jacaranda blossoms outside the old shed, the air cool and sweet with the scent of damp earth and woodsmoke. He spent the morning quietly organizing his cedar shelf, arranging his brass compass and sea-glass beside the clay bird whistle and the small spool of indigo wool. Each item held a memory of the long road behind him, from the misty heights of Cloudveil Ridge all the way down into this quiet southern valley.

Stepping out into the crisp morning air, James followed the dirt lane past weathered adobe walls toward the center of Aldea San Gabriel. He greeted a stray ginger cat sleeping on a cracked tile roof, watched a pair of mourning doves take flight from a stone trough, and listened to the distant, rhythmic ring of this man's hammer striking chisel at the open-air workshop. The village was waking slowly to its daily rhythms, unhurried and peaceful beneath the expansive blue sky.

Returning to the workshop, James found this man carefully planing a strip of cedar, sending pale curls of fragrant wood spilling across the workbench. Without a word, this man handed James a small wooden offcut and a piece of coarse sandpaper, inviting him to smooth the edge. James sat on a low wooden stool, rubbing the wood in steady, rhythmic circles until the surface felt as smooth as polished river stone.

As the midday sun climbed high above the valley, casting sharp shadows across the dusty lanes, James felt a quiet sense of belonging settle deep into his chest. He was no longer just passing through on an endless journey with no map, but a part of this small, forgotten place. Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next, he thought quietly as he placed his finished piece of wood alongside this man's tools on the workbench.
location: Don Tadeo's workshop, Aldea San Gabriel
